hints.title: Linear Auxiliary Allocation Obstacle
hints.text: Copying all node values to an array consumes linear auxiliary space. How can finding the midpoint and inverting the latter half allow symmetric comparison in O(1) space?

hints.title: Half-List In-Place Inversion Invariant
hints.text: Locate the list midpoint, reverse the second half in-place, and compare corresponding nodes from both ends inward.

hints.title: Midpoint Split and Inward Check Procedure
hints.text: Use slow and fast to reach the midpoint. Reverse the list starting from slow. Compare nodes starting from head and reversed half until the second half ends. Return true if all match, else false.

hints.title: Complete Implementation
hints.text:
```python
class Solution:
    def isPalindrome(self, head: Optional[ListNode]) -> bool:
        if not head or not head.next:
            return True
        slow = head
        fast = head
        while fast and fast.next:
            slow = slow.next
            fast = fast.next.next
        prev = None
        curr = slow
        while curr:
            nxt = curr.next
            curr.next = prev
            prev = curr
            curr = nxt
        p1 = head
        p2 = prev
        while p2:
            if p1.val != p2.val:
                return False
            p1 = p1.next
            p2 = p2.next
        return True
```

variables: N: number of nodes in list (1 <= N <= 10^5)
complexity.notes: Find midpoint, reverse second half in-place, and compare in O(1) auxiliary space.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Buffering node values in a dynamic array requires O(N) extra memory, failing the O(1) follow-up challenge.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: In-place half-reversal achieves O(1) auxiliary space with only two linear passes.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Ability to find the midpoint with fast/slow pointers and reverse a sublist cleanly.
